Plot posterior hindcasts and forecasts

Source: R/plot.mvgam_forecast.R
plot.mvgam_forecast.Rd

Plot method for mvgam_forecast objects returned by hindcast.mvgam() and forecast.mvgam(). Draws one panel per series (faceted by default) with nested quantile ribbons for the forecast, a single grey ribbon for the hindcast, posterior median lines and the observations as points. A dashed vertical line marks the boundary between training and forecast times when both are drawn.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam_forecast
plot(
  x,
  series = NULL,
  probs = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95),
  hindcast = TRUE,
  forecast = TRUE,
  newdata_obs = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An mvgam_forecast object.

series

Optional integer vector, character vector of series names, or "all". When NULL (the default), every series is plotted and the panels are faceted via ggplot2::facet_wrap().

probs

Numeric vector of credible interval widths for the forecast ribbon. Defaults to c(0.5, 0.8, 0.95) which draws three nested bands from the outer 95% to the inner 50%. Hindcast ribbons always use the widest entry.

hindcast, forecast

Logical. Whether the hindcast and the forecast are drawn. Both default to TRUE. Setting one to FALSE draws the other alone.

newdata_obs

Logical. When TRUE (the default) and the object carries test_observations, the test observations are overlaid on the forecast region.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

The forecast takes the shades of the red bayesplot scheme. The hindcast band is light grey, which separates in-sample uncertainty from the nested forecast bands.

For state-extrapolating prediction over arbitrary newdata see forecast.mvgam() and hindcast.mvgam(); for marginal-MC prediction see posterior_predict.mvgam() / posterior_epred.mvgam().

See also
